name: ACCEL Middle College (East Side Union / Evergreen Valley College)
org: East Side Union High School District
what_you_do: Sophomores and juniors attend college classes in the morning at Evergreen Valley College and high school classes in the afternoon.
who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)
deadline_text: Recruitment meetings are held in the evening; dates not posted on the page I read.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).

name: Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth)
what_you_do: Help getting into college, jobs and work-based learning like internships and apprenticeships, with mentoring and support services.
grades: Currently in high school or college
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.
deadline_text: Ongoing
how_to_apply: Contact a regional provider: Eden Area ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. Main ACWDB line: (510) 259-3842.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead: La Familia (Eden Area) (925) 935-2643, Ohlone College (Tri Cities) (510) 742-2323, International Rescue Committee (North Cities) (510) 857-6884.

name: Alameda County Youth Innovation Program
what_you_do: Help preparing for college and jobs, including internships and apprenticeships, plus work experience, mentoring, career counseling and financial literacy.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who are currently in high school or college. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use a separate county youth program.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Services include paid and unpaid work experience, so ask the provider about pay.
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the program page: Eden ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. County line: 510-259-3842.
notes: Two providers only: Eden ROP (Hayward) and Tri-Valley ROP (Livermore), so which one serves you depends on where you live. Pay is not stated. A Hayward AJCC fact sheet (Rubicon Programs) mentions federal WIOA youth ages 14 to 24 with at least one barrier; ask your provider about younger teens.

name: American Legion Auxiliary California Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
what_you_do: A one-week summer leadership session for 11th grade girls, run by the American Legion Auxiliary. Each delegate is chosen and sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit. The pages read do not describe the daily activities.
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grader during the 2025-26 school year)
who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade who are selected and sponsored by a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Each high school may have only one delegate. If a school has no sponsoring Unit, a student can apply as a Department (statewide) alternate applicant. Age rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22-27, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 22-27, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadlines are not posted on the site.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion Boys & Girls State program in ca-boys-girls-state.json (no separate Boys State card was made). The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages read.

name: Alameda County Community Food Bank: Volunteer
what_you_do: Sign up for volunteer shifts at the food bank warehouse in Oakland. Tasks and times are listed on the volunteer calendar.
who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick a shift on the volunteer calendar.
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.

name: Alameda County Library Teen Volunteers (Fremont, Newark, Union City)
city: Fremont, Newark and Union City, CA
what_you_do: Teens can find volunteer roles at Alameda County Library branches through its Better Impact portal.
who_can_apply: Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal. Not stated on the page I read.
deadline_text: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. Phone 510-745-1500. The application link is on the official page.
notes: The teen page is thin. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
what_you_do: Teens suggest ideas for library events and projects. 1 service hour per meeting.
who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
pay_detail: Community service hours only
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
deadline_text: Rolling
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO)
what_you_do: Write teen book reviews (1 service hour each, one a month) or help younger kids with LEGO coding activities.
who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
pay_detail: Community service hours only
deadline_text: Rolling
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the Teen Book Reviews page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO.

name: Alameda Youth Career and Job Fair
org: City of Alameda and Alameda Unified School District
what_you_do: Free fair where students meet employers, schools, nonprofits and trade groups to explore careers, part-time jobs, internships and training.
who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education (CTE) programs.
pay_detail: Free event
deadline_text: The 10th annual fair was Wednesday, April 1, 2026, 1 to 5 pm. No 2027 date is posted.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.

name: TRIO Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math and Science (American River College)
what_you_do: Free tutoring, academic advising, college application and financial aid help, campus visits and career exploration, with monthly Saturday Academies and a required summer part.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.
duration: Year-round, including a required summer component
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read, so ask staff for current dates.

name: BART Summer Internship (high school)
what_you_do: Paid summer internship at BART, 10 to 20 hours a week, in person.
who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 program ran June 22 to July 31, 2026. Direct applications are not accepted. 2027 not posted.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.

name: Berkeley High CTE Pathways
what_you_do: Career pathways at Berkeley High in six areas: health, public service, arts and media, IT, engineering, and building trades. Students can earn credit for an internship or work-based learning.
who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
deadline_text: Choose pathway classes during course selection.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g college entry requirements. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.

name: Berkeley Humane Volunteer (teens 12 and up)
what_you_do: Help in the thrift shop, at adoption events, in the vet clinic, with foster care or with office work after a volunteer orientation.
who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
deadline_text: Rolling. Internships are 18+ only.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

name: Berkeley Pre-College Scholars (Summer Sessions)
what_you_do: Take UC Berkeley summer classes for college credit in a 6 or 8 week session.
who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 2 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.

name: Berkeley Public Library Teen Volunteer and Youth Worker
what_you_do: Volunteer at a Berkeley library (Teen Volunteer Application), or work as a paid Youth Worker, up to 15 hours a week, hired through Berkeley YouthWorks.
who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application (no age stated). Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25, no experience needed; a work permit is required if under 18.
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Youth Worker jobs are paid (rate not posted; no benefits).
duration: Youth Worker up to 15 hours a week
deadline_text: Library page says YouthWorks accepts applications in March and October only. YouthWorks lists a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks may require Berkeley residency.

name: Teen Council
org: Berkeley Repertory Theatre, School of Theatre
what_you_do: 10 to 15 Bay Area high schoolers plan Teen Night programs, host original works showcases, organize advocacy events and interview artists.
who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
pay_detail: Transportation stipend. Free admission to teen programs and shows, and free food at events.
deadline_text: A new group is chosen at the start of each school year. No 2026 to 2027 dates are posted; join the mailing list for news.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.

name: Berkeley YouthWorks
what_you_do: Paid, part-time, temporary internships through the City of Berkeley, plus a Ready to Work workshop series that pays a stipend.
who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
pay_detail: Wage not posted. Ready to Work workshop stipend if you attend at least 7 of 8 sessions.
duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027
deadline_text: Interest form for Winter 2027 is due October 30, 2026. Summer 2027 information is expected February 2027. Fall 2026 is full through November 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.

name: Beyond Emancipation (B:E) employment coaching for foster youth
what_you_do: Coaching for current and former foster youth on career interests, resumes, budgeting, job connections, and training or apprenticeship options.
who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages read.
pay_detail: No pay to the youth is stated. The cost of services to the youth is not stated on the pages read.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No application window is stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left null or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.

name: Junior Staff (Boys & Girls Clubs of Oakland)
what_you_do: Club teens who meet the requirements take paid work positions at the Club. The page says these give real work experience and professional development.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
pay_detail: The page says 'Paid positions and income.' The pay rate and hours are not stated.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Work permit rules for paid work under 18 apply in California; the page does not say whether one is needed here.

name: Black Girls Code Workshops
what_you_do: Workshops in robotics, art and AI for girls ages 7 to 18, plus free Code Along videos on YouTube and mentoring chances.
who_can_apply: Girls ages 7 to 18 for workshops. A separate College and Careers Community serves ages 18 plus.
pay_detail: Prices not posted; Code Along videos are free
deadline_text: See the events page for current workshops.
how_to_apply: Check the community events page for current workshops: community.wearebgc.org/events.
notes: The home page did not name a Bay Area chapter, prices or workshop dates. Check the events page for what is open now. Code Along videos are free on YouTube.

name: Teaching Intern and Summer Volunteer
what_you_do: Teach and tutor middle schoolers in a six-week summer program after 80 hours of training. The site says college and high school students serve as teachers.
who_can_apply: The site says it recruits college and high school students as teaching interns. No age or grade rule is posted. Middle school students can also join as program students.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.
deadline_text: Not posted.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.

name: American Legion California Boys & Girls State
what_you_do: Week-long summer program at Sacramento State where students who finished junior year run a mock state government. Open to all genders since 2023.
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application: your school recommends you and a local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs: this one is coed since 2023. American Legion Auxiliary California Girls State (cagirlsstate.org) is its own program, ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. Old note about a 2020 article and Sanger phone was out of date.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
what_you_do: Teens in Explorer posts train in law enforcement skills and can compete at the CHP statewide Explorer competition, held at the CHP Academy in West Sacramento. Contact CHP to find a post.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet (this is the competition age rule). Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages read.
pay_detail: No pay stated. 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 24 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
what_you_do: The state agency that registers apprenticeships. Use its search tool to find registered apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs near you.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
what_you_do: Volunteer or student intern roles at state parks. People under 18 can volunteer with written parent or guardian permission.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
pay_detail: Unpaid
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
what_you_do: School-supervised work or job-sampling that earns credit. Exploratory WEE is unpaid career sampling (can start at age 12). General and Career Technical WEE are paid jobs with a related class.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a CTE class you take.
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: Youth clubs and projects in science, agriculture, leadership and community service, with teen leader roles.
who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
what_you_do: Learn agriculture in class, run a hands-on Supervised Agricultural Experience (a job or project), and build leadership through events.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
what_you_do: A three-year 'school within a school' for grades 10 to 12 that mixes academics with a career focus, business mentors and internships.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy sets its own application. Search the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Counted as school credit.
deadline_text: Application is through the school that hosts the academy.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy, or check nearby high schools. Whether students from other districts may transfer in depends on the district's open enrollment rules.
notes: The CDE site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (bot check), so this card could not be re-confirmed against the official page. Grades 10 to 12 and the school-within-a-school model need confirming. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Supporting Student Success (WIOA In-School Youth)
org: Contra Costa County Office of Education
city: Contra Costa County, CA (West County and East County)
what_you_do: Case management, career exploration and paid workforce preparation and work experience for high school students who qualify.
who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Ongoing
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.

name: Chabot College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
what_you_do: Tuition-free Individual Dual Enrollment (classes at Chabot or online), CCAP classes at your high school, and a summer academy.
who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, complete the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: cc-earlycollege@chabotcollege.edu or 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.

name: Galaxy Explorers Program
what_you_do: A three-year STEM and workforce program. Teens work museum floor shifts explaining science, join inquiry teams on engineering and tech projects, and can take leadership roles in later years.
grades: Typically enters the summer before 10th grade and stays through 12th grade
who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated, so needs_work_permit is null.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
what_you_do: Explorer post for teens who want a law enforcement career, with training and mentoring from CHP officers.
who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post.

name: FARMS Leadership Program
what_you_do: School-year cohort that visits farms, conservation sites, ag businesses and colleges (at least six field days) and builds resume, interview and speaking skills.
who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.

name: Urban Ag Internships
what_you_do: Year-long paid internship at a school garden: weekly garden hours, a workforce class, field trips to farms and guest speakers.
who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.

name: College of San Mateo Dual Enrollment and Concurrent Enrollment
what_you_do: Take free college classes at College of San Mateo while in high school. Dual enrollment (through partner high schools) includes free books and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units a semester.
who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.
deadline_text: No application deadline stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).

name: Computer History Museum Teen Volunteer Intern Program
what_you_do: Teens in grades 9 to 12 go behind the scenes with the education team, research tech history, meet Silicon Valley professionals and lead tours and activities.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: Applications are currently closed. Join the interest list to hear about the next round.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.

name: Congressional App Challenge
what_you_do: Build an app in any language and submit it to your House district. Winners are shown at the US Capitol.
who_can_apply: Middle or high school students living in the US (citizenship not required). Solo or teams up to four. Half the team must live in the district.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline for registering and submitting is October 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Register on the Student Registration page, then submit the app online.
notes: Any language or platform is allowed, solo or teams up to four. Check the Participating Districts page on the site to confirm your district takes part.

name: Contra Costa College Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Free college classes (no tuition, books or enrollment fees) for students of West Contra Costa USD (including Middle College High School on campus), Leadership Public Schools and Griffin Technology Academies.
who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.

name: Contra Costa County Library Teen Volunteers
city: Contra Costa County, CA (Richmond, Concord, Pleasant Hill and other branches)
what_you_do: Teen roles include Summer Read volunteer, Computer Docent and Homework Help.
grades: Entering 8th grade or above (Summer Read); age 16+ for other roles
who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
duration: Summer Read 1 to 2 hours a week; Computer Docents at least 2 hours a week
deadline_text: Summer Read recruiting starts in April. Some libraries take volunteers on a limited basis.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.

name: COSMOS (California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science) at UC Davis
what_you_do: Four-week residential summer program with college-level math and science courses and hands-on projects.
who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
pay_detail: Program cost $5,793 (2027 page), plus $48 application fee and a 2.5% card fee. Financial aid is available for admitted students with need, but not guaranteed.
deadline_text: Application opens Jan 6, 2027 at 8:00 AM and closes Feb 5, 2027 (dates page says 5:00 PM). Financial aid forms postmarked by Feb 6, 2027. Decisions Mar 25, 2027.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos

name: Teen Action Academy and Teen Leadership Committee
what_you_do: Teen Action Academy (grades 9 to 12) plans service projects and teen events. Teen Leadership Committee (grades 7 to 8) builds leadership and teamwork.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
deadline_text: Not posted on the volunteer page.
how_to_apply: No steps are posted. Email MadisonLeeRosen@CosumnesCSD.gov, call the District at 916-405-5600, or fill out the General Volunteer Interest Form on cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.

name: Cosumnes Fire Department Explorer Program
org: Cosumnes Community Services District Fire Department
what_you_do: Classroom and hands-on training in fire and EMS, with leadership practice and community service hours.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
deadline_text: Applications for the next school year open in Spring 2027 (no exact date or closing date posted).
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.

name: CPMC Information Desk Volunteer (Van Ness Campus, Sutter Health)
org: Sutter Health, California Pacific Medical Center (CPMC)
city: San Francisco, CA (CPMC Van Ness Campus, 1101 Van Ness Avenue)
what_you_do: Greet visitors and patients in the main lobby of CPMC Van Ness Campus. Give directions, information and help at the front desk.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the listing
duration: Minimum 100 hours in one year, at least three to four hours per week
deadline_text: The listing shows Actively Recruiting. No application deadline is stated.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.

name: Cupertino Teen Commission
what_you_do: Teen commissioners advise the Cupertino City Council on issues that affect local youth. They attend monthly meetings from September to May.
who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are incoming 8th to 11th graders. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
deadline_text: The city page says recruitment is currently closed. No reopening date is stated.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday, in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term; the 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.

name: Lifeguard Training, Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor
what_you_do: Take Red Cross lifeguard training, a junior lifeguard class, or Junior Swim Instructor (shadowing instructors), which can lead to volunteer chances and city aquatics jobs.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the course. Junior Lifeguarding: pass a swim skills check on day one (25 yards of front crawl and breaststroke, tread water 1 minute, and more). Junior Swim Instructor: no age or swim test listed on the page.
pay_detail: Course fees apply. Amounts are not on the page; check the Rec Guide or online registration.
deadline_text: Courses are offered throughout the year. Check WebTrac for sessions.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Training can lead to City of Davis aquatics work. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later, with volunteer chances after the training. The page does not promise a job. Lifeguard certification needs full attendance and passing tests. Job minimum ages are set in each posting at cityofdavis.org/jobs.

name: Davis Senior High CTE Pathways
what_you_do: School classes in career pathways inside seven industry sectors, taught in a sequence of courses. The district also offers student internships through its CTE program.
who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Enroll through your counselor during normal course selection.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab (see the Internship and Career Development Course).
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.

name: Teen Leadership Council
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
what_you_do: Plan events and service projects, learn leadership skills and speak up on issues that matter to Davis teens.
who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period was extended to Oct 2, 2026 and is now closed. The next call is not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.

name: De Anza College Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Take De Anza College classes, online or on campus, while in high school. Many courses count toward CSU or UC credit.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply for admission before the quarter you want; see the De Anza academic calendar.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.

name: DECA (high school division)
what_you_do: School clubs that prepare students for marketing, finance, hospitality and management careers, with competitions and conferences.
who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.
deadline_text: Join anytime through your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.

name: Internship and Career Development Course
what_you_do: School course with weekly coaching on resumes, cover letters and interviews. You get an unpaid internship placement or prep for paid work. Sites include Davis Public Library, Davis Vanguard, Mercy General and Pemberton Engineering.
who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. 2026-27 sites are listed now.
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.

name: Dublin L.E.A.D. Summer Program
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
what_you_do: Teens assist City of Dublin camp staff during summer camps and swim lessons. They get training in job skills, leading activities, water safety, and supervising campers.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.

name: Dublin Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
what_you_do: Dublin teens give the City input on its programs and activities for young people. The committee meets monthly, usually on the second Wednesday at the Dublin Senior Center.
grades: Enrolled in middle school or high school
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 seats are filled (term June 2026 to May 2027). The city page we read does not post a recruitment date for the 2027-28 term.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page we read. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.

name: EBAYC Volunteers and Student Internships
what_you_do: Volunteer and student internship options at a youth group that offers life coaching, school partnerships and community organizing.
who_can_apply: Not stated.
deadline_text: Not posted
how_to_apply: The home page links to a volunteer page on ebayc.org. Contact EBAYC directly.
notes: The home page says it welcomes volunteers, volunteer groups and student internships but gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it did not load (404) on Oct 7, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

name: EBMUD High School Summer Internship (HSSI)
city: Oakland, CA and EBMUD service area
what_you_do: Paid 6 week summer internship (about 16 hours a week) at the water utility.
who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 East Bay program: no direct applications, referrals from partner groups only. 2027 not posted.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.

name: East Bay Regional Park District Youth and Student Jobs
city: Oakland, CA and parks across Alameda and Contra Costa counties
what_you_do: Seasonal paid student jobs such as recreation leader, lifeguard, gate attendant, student laborer and interpretive student aide, with pathways from high school to college.
who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.
deadline_text: No jobs were posted on governmentjobs.com on Oct 7, 2026. Watch ebparks.org/jobs/youth and governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.

name: Youth Environmental Academy and Internships
what_you_do: After-school environmental justice program for Berkeley teens and young adults (8 weeks in summer or 12 weeks in spring). Topics include zero waste, climate resilience and food systems. Paid.
who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
pay_detail: Paid; rate not posted
deadline_text: No dates on the Ecology Center page. Berkeley YouthWorks listed a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026 and said Summer 2027 information comes in Feb 2027, but that page does not mention this academy.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.

name: Eden Area ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
what_you_do: Career classes taken in high school at the Eden Area ROP center in Hayward or at some home schools. Pathways include welding, auto, construction, culinary, dental assisting, cybersecurity, first responder and education careers.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
duration: Classes are held Monday to Friday; course length varies by class
deadline_text: Enroll through your home school counselor; the page gives no class start dates.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.

name: El Camino Health Junior Auxiliary
city: Mountain View and Los Gatos, CA
what_you_do: A year-long hospital volunteer program for teens in Mountain View and Los Gatos.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. Competitive, with limited spots. No summer-only option.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page
deadline_text: No application deadline posted. The page says to check back in mid-January 2027 for signup for the next Junior Application Seminar.
how_to_apply: Attend the annual application seminar, then apply. Info on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Hospital does not offer summer-only or programs shorter than one year. Locations are Mountain View and Los Gatos. Spots are limited (earlier check).

name: Elk Grove Youth Commission
what_you_do: Advise the City Council on youth needs. Commissioners meet monthly, meet with their Councilmember, plan youth events and report to the Council.
who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers
deadline_text: No open recruitment as of Oct 7, 2026. Seats are filled when openings come up, and the City posts a notice with a Youth Commission application.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages read, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens.

name: Evergreen Valley College Dual Enrollment and CCAP
what_you_do: Take free college classes while in high school: open classes at your own choice (up to 11 units, 7 in summer) or cohort classes at partner high schools (CCAP, up to 15 units a semester).
who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED, with approval from your school counselor or principal. Adult school students in GED programs can also join.
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.

name: Exploring (Learning for Life career posts)
what_you_do: Career exploration posts in 12 fields such as health care, law enforcement, fire and EMS, engineering, and law and government, with hands-on activities.
who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line.

name: High School Internships (Facciotti Lab)
what_you_do: Local high school students work on computational and wet-lab research after school and in summer.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.
deadline_text: No application process or dates posted.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.

name: Trailblazers -N- Training
org: City of Folsom Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: Leadership training (decision-making, conflict resolution, teamwork), then you volunteer with campers ages 6 to 10 in the Destination Recreation summer camp. You get a T-shirt and a Friday lunch.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
deadline_text: 2026 post went up May 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.

name: Foothill College High School Dual Enrollment
city: Los Altos Hills and Sunnyvale, CA
what_you_do: Take real Foothill College classes for college and high school credit while in high school, on campus, online, or at Sunnyvale Center. Free up to 11 units a quarter.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.
deadline_text: No single deadline stated. Submit the form before you register each quarter.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).

name: Forage Virtual Job Simulations
what_you_do: Free, self-paced online job simulations that copy real work tasks and let you compare your answers to model answers. Over 250 simulations from more than 90 employers.
who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Always open.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.

name: Fremont Unified Career and Technical Education
what_you_do: CTE courses at middle and high schools in 15 sectors and 58 pathways, some inside California Partnership Academies or regional occupational programs.
who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining CTE programs.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No dates stated. Choose courses at your school.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general: 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways, and it does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.

name: Genesys Works Bay Area Internship Program
what_you_do: Eight weeks of business technology and professional skills training, then a paid, year-long internship at a partner company, plus college and career coaching.
who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
deadline_text: No dates posted. Applicants get an interview, then summer skills training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages read. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.

name: Girls Inc. of Alameda County High School Programs
city: Oakland, CA (and Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
what_you_do: Free programs for high school girls: coding (Code the Game, grades 10 to 12), college access, leadership, and paid summer internships at Bay Area companies.
who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact Girls Inc.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: Code the Game is a six week program (the page mentions a fall offering). Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.

name: Girls Who Code Clubs and Pathways
what_you_do: Free coding clubs (grades 3 to 12, after school or weekends) and a free self-paced online Pathways program for high school students.
grades: Clubs: grades 3 to 12 (split 3 to 5 and 6 to 12). Pathways: high school.
who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
deadline_text: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
what_you_do: Build or repair affordable homes on construction sites; younger teens can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch.
who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page
deadline_text: Ongoing. No sign-up deadline stated.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
what_you_do: Help build and repair homes on a job site, or work in the ReStore organizing, pricing and stocking items, after a one hour orientation. Training, tools and safety gear are provided.
who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)
deadline_text: Rolling. Sign up for shifts after orientation.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

name: Hack Club
what_you_do: Free teen coding community with school clubs, an online Slack, game jams, hackathons and hardware events.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Join anytime.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
what_you_do: October event with online challenges, livestreams and over 500 local in-person fests. This year it focuses on open source and open-weight AI.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Runs through October 2026; sign in with MyMLH.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)
what_you_do: Monthly volunteer projects open to younger volunteers, found on the HandsOn Community Calendar. The 2-week HandsOn Tomorrow summer program (up to 40 hours) is not running in summer 2026.
grades: High school (for HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Council)
who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
deadline_text: Monthly projects: sign up on the Community Calendar. HandsOn Tomorrow will not run in summer 2026 and no later dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow is paused (no summer 2026 session) and the Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
what_you_do: Teens do animal meet-and-greets, help with animal care routines and work as camp helpers. Good for future zookeepers and vet techs.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps but is not required.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed seasonally. The last orientation listed on the page was Oct 18, 2025 (old); no 2026-27 date is posted.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

name: H.A.R.D. Volunteer Program (Hayward Area Recreation and Park District)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
what_you_do: Volunteer at district events and ongoing service projects such as senior programs, nature programs, special needs programs and theatre ushering. Teens can earn community service hours and work experience.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.
deadline_text: Opportunities are posted throughout the year. No closing date is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

name: Hayward Public Library Teen Volunteer Opportunities
what_you_do: Teens help the Children's Room librarians with tasks like cleaning books and craft prep, in 1-hour shifts. Teens can also attend Teen Library Council meetings.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted during the school year. No closing date is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.

name: Hayward Youth Commission
what_you_do: Youth commissioners advise the Hayward City Council, the Hayward Area Recreation and Park District and the Hayward Unified School District on issues that affect young people, and work on youth projects.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall on the second Monday of each month, September to June, except holidays. The 2021 notice said two-year terms.
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday, May 9, 2025. Interviews were on Friday, May 30, 2025. No 2026 cycle was found.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

name: Hidden Genius Project Immersion Program
what_you_do: Free 15 month program (800+ hours): two 7-week summers plus a year of after-school sessions in coding, entrepreneurship and leadership, for Black male high school students.
who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed
deadline_text: The application page says applications are currently closed and to follow HGP social media or the newsletter for the 2027 application. The last posted deadline was Feb 21, 2025.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The immersion page still shows the old 2025 deadline. No 2027 date is posted, so wait for the new announcement. Oakland and Richmond are the East Bay sites.

name: Hiller Aviation Museum Flight Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens run hands-on STEM stations like Imagination Playground and virtual reality for visitors on alternating weekend days.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
what_you_do: Student group for health science students with skills contests, leadership events and health career exploration.
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Students under 18 can foster cats or dogs at home with a parent or guardian, or make no-sew fleece blankets for shelter animals, and earn service hours.
who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

name: JA Launchpad (Junior Achievement, Fremont)
what_you_do: A new Fremont career education center with a money-management simulation (JA Finance Park), a student business program (JA Company Program) and career summits with mentors from companies.
who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)
deadline_text: The page says the center is Coming Early 2027. No opening date or sign-up is posted.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free live-in career training with pre-apprenticeship tracks (construction, carpentry, cement masonry) and Certified Nurse Assistant, plus high school or GED help.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
