notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Book Reviewer)
what_you_do: Teens ages 12 to 18 can join Teens Reach to help plan library activities, or earn service hours by writing book reviews as a Teen Book Reviewer.
who_can_apply: The page lists teen programs for ages 12 to 18. A minimum age for general volunteering is not stated. Sign up through the volunteer page and an orientation (on-site or virtual).
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Use "Sign Up to Volunteer" on the library volunteer page and the Better Impact system, and attend an orientation. Email volunteer@sjlibrary.org.
notes: Teen Book Reviewer roles are listed on Better Impact. See also the separate Teens Reach card.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
what_you_do: Paid work experience and job help for San Jose youth. Teens ages 14 to 18 with barriers to work get placed in paid jobs and training; ages 16 to 29 get job services.
who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages I read. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
what_you_do: Teens advise the San Jose Mayor and City Council on youth issues. The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is open now; Youth Commission recruitment is closed.
who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20, must live in the district they represent, two-year term (up to two terms), meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council: no deadline posted. Youth Commission: recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the District Youth Advisory Application for the YAC. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
what_you_do: Free job-skills workshops, a members-only job and internship board, and twenty $2,000 scholarships a year for San Mateo County youth. The county summer internship is for ages 18 to 21.
who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens shelve books, help with kids' crafts and STEM programs, join outreach events or support the makerspace.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).

name: Santa Clara County Teen CERT Academy
what_you_do: A weekend emergency response course (fire safety, search and rescue, stop the bleed, disaster psychology) after which teens can help their community in disasters. Earn 20+ volunteer hours.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.

name: County of Santa Clara Intern and Earn
org: County of Santa Clara Employment Connection
what_you_do: An eight week paid county internship plus job-readiness workshops, hiring events and coaching from an Employment Counselor. Interns work up to 30 hours a week.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers (tutor a K-6 student)
what_you_do: Teens 14 and older can volunteer with the Santa Clara County Library District, including tutoring a kindergarten to grade 6 student after school.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card.

name: County of Santa Clara Student Internship Program (Level I, high school)
org: County of Santa Clara Employee Services Agency
what_you_do: High school students can work as paid student interns in county departments, helping professional staff under close supervision. Tasks depend on the department.
grades: High school (regular, vocational or working toward equivalency)
who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).
deadline_text: No current posting for Level I. Subscribe to email alerts on the Student Intern, Level I job title or contact county departments. Applications are reviewed as departments ask and expire after 6 months.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor
city: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga, CA
what_you_do: Teens tutor kindergarten to grade 6 students with homework help after school at a library. You can earn community service hours.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older, free one afternoon Monday to Thursday from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester, and about 7 hours of training.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application on the library's volunteer page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is included. Training is online (about 7 hours).

name: Sacramento County Office of Education Career Technical Education
what_you_do: County CTE courses across 15 industry sectors that mix technical training with academics. A course catalog is posted on the SCOE CTE site.
who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
deadline_text: Course catalog online; no student deadline posted on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.

name: 826 Valencia Youth Programs
what_you_do: Free after-school writing help, workshops, summer programs and college and leadership support. SFPL lists stipended leadership and writing roles for grades 8 to 12.
grades: Programs for ages 6 to 18; stipended roles for grades 8 to 12
who_can_apply: Students ages 6 to 18. Many students join through partner schools; some workshops allow direct sign-up.
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)
deadline_text: No dates posted. Check the 826 Valencia program calendar.
how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.

name: Breakthrough Leadership Program (BLP)
what_you_do: High school students serve as role models for middle schoolers in a summer program: co-teach an elective like dance or soccer, help with after-school tutoring, lead cheers and plan events.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student (grades 9 to 12). Preference goes to current Breakthrough students and current or former Breakthrough volunteers.
pay_detail: Paid through San Francisco's Opportunities for All program (rate not posted on the page). Some hours also count toward school volunteer requirements.
duration: Summer 2026 ran orientation June 15 to 18, then June 22 to July 31, 2026, about 6 weeks
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says the summer 2027 application launches in early 2027; exact dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.

name: Careers in Science (CiS) Intern Program
what_you_do: Multi-year, year-round paid internship where teens do fieldwork, teach visitors, and join research projects, after school and on Saturdays.
who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027; closing date not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.

name: CCSF Dual Enrollment (free college classes)
org: City College of San Francisco and SFUSD
what_you_do: Take free City College classes while in high school and earn both high school and college credit.
who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Ask your counselor before each term.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.

name: Community Youth Center Youth Job Fair
org: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
what_you_do: One-day job fair for youth looking for work: meet employers, learn about openings, get resume help, practice interviews, take headshots and get free professional clothing.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
pay_detail: Free event
deadline_text: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. at Stonestown Galleria.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.

name: High School Elections Ambassador Program
what_you_do: Learn how to plan and run pre-registration events that help 16 and 17 year olds sign up to vote. Includes an in-person training and a mentor from the Department of Elections.
who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed (the round ran Sept 14 to 27, 2026). The program runs twice a year, in April and September. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.
notes: Same page: if you will be 16 by the next Election Day you can apply to be a high school poll worker, with a stipend up to $245. A poll worker application for the November 2026 election was due to be posted there in mid-August.

name: High School Explainer Program
what_you_do: Paid museum job: help visitors at exhibits, lead demonstrations such as cow's eye dissections, and help run museum operations. More than 60 hours of training.
who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
deadline_text: School-year applications are typically posted in July and summer applications in March. Closing dates are not stated.
how_to_apply: When open, apply on the Exploratorium Current Openings page under the job title High School Explainer. Questions: hsesupervisors@exploratorium.edu.
notes: About 130 paid positions a year across two cohorts. The Current Openings list did not show on my read, so check it for a live posting. A separate PACE program serves ages 17 to 21.

name: San Francisco Fire Youth Academy
what_you_do: Free Saturday program that teaches basic firefighting and EMS skills, CPR and first aid, plus life skills like financial literacy, leadership and time management.
who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., following the SFUSD calendar. A 2025 news article said 15 weeks each fall.
deadline_text: Not stated on the academy's site. A 2025 news article reported an Aug 11, 2025 deadline for the fall class.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. Because it pays a stipend, ask whether a work permit is needed. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association.

name: Girls on the Run Bay Area Junior Coach
org: Girls on the Run Bay Area
what_you_do: Coach elementary and middle school girls in a running and life-skills program as a junior coach, 1.5 to 3 hours a week for 8 to 10 weeks.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and in high school. The page says teens on Heart&Sole teams must identify as female, and males are welcome on Girls on the Run teams. Needs a completed reference, a signed waiver (parent signs if under 18) and the Junior Coach application. Background check at 18.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026
deadline_text: The fall 2026 Junior Coach application was due Aug 26, 2026 (season started early September; 5K on Nov 14, 2026). Spring dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Coach application on the Girls on the Run Bay Area site. Email admin@gotrbayarea.org or call (415) 863-8942 to ask about late spots or the next season.
notes: The Oct 12, 2026 date on the sf.gov listing is for adult coaches (18 and up), not Junior Coaches. Teams meet at least once a week.

name: Mission Bit Free Coding Classes
what_you_do: Free semester-long coding and computer science classes for high schoolers, in person or remote, plus workshops, self-paced courses and events.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 (high school). Priority goes to youth underrepresented in tech, students at high schools with few or no computer science classes, and girls and LGBTQIA+ youth. Online classes are for San Francisco students only.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Semester long. Fall 2026 classes ran Sep 8 to Dec 4, 2026.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 class registration is closed. Spring 2027 classes are not posted yet. Workshops and events are posted separately (College Connections is Nov 7, 2026).
how_to_apply: Pick a class and register on the Mission Bit Classes page when registration opens.
notes: Mission Bit's Tech Start career prep is ages 18 to 26, not for most high schoolers. College Connections (Nov 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to noon at Chase Center, grades 9 to 12) closes registration Oct 27, 2026 per sf.gov.

name: Mayor's Youth Employment and Education Program (MYEEP)
org: Japanese Community Youth Council (JCYC), funded by SF DCYF; Buchanan YMCA is a partner site
what_you_do: Job readiness training and paid work experience for younger teens, plus homework help and mentoring.
who_can_apply: San Francisco youth ages 14 to 17 (the DCYF newsletter lists grades 9 and 10 for this round). Apply through the JCYC Workhub.
pay_detail: Paid work experience (hourly rate not posted on the pages read)
duration: School year: Oct to April, with an 8 hour per week internship Jan to April. Summer: June to August, 20 hours per week.
deadline_text: School-year round closed Sept 14, 2026. The YMCA page says summer applications are due the first week of April; school-year applications the first week of September.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the JCYC Workhub (jcycworkhub.org). Ask the YMCA contact on the program page about your neighborhood site.
notes: Pay rate is not stated on the pages read, so ask your site. Contact the Buchanan YMCA ((415) 931-9622) about eligibility.

name: New Door Ventures Employment Program
what_you_do: Six month paid internships with employer partners, plus job coaching, for young people who are out of school or work.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Aimed at 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or not working.
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Applications accepted all year (per the sf.gov youth listing).
how_to_apply: Apply on the New Door intake portal linked from their site. The application link is on the official page.
notes: Mainly for 17 year olds and older who are not in a regular school path; not the usual fit for a student who is in school. Pay is not stated on the pages read.

name: Opportunities for All (OFA) and Black 2 San Francisco
org: San Francisco Human Rights Commission, with JCYC
what_you_do: Paid summer internships with local organizations and businesses, plus career workshops and mentorship. Black 2 San Francisco is a separate 6 week program for 30 students.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 24 who live in or go to school in San Francisco (that is the only rule on the OFA page).
pay_detail: Paid; the hourly rate and hours are not posted on the pages read
duration: B2SF is 6 weeks; OFA length not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: The 2026 OFA deadline was April 10, 2026. The summer application is closed; 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the JCYC Workhub, complete the application and submit before the spring deadline.
notes: Applications are run by JCYC. B2SF and the OFA fellowships share an application with other youth programs. Interest areas decide placement.

name: California Pre-Register to Vote (ages 16 and 17)
what_you_do: Sign up early so you are on the voter list the day you turn 18. Pairs well with the SF elections ambassador program.
who_can_apply: California residents ages 16 and 17 who are US citizens and not in prison for a felony or ruled mentally unable to vote by a court.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Always open.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form at registertovote.ca.gov (linked from the Secretary of State page).
notes: Not a job or internship, but a real civic step. Your registration becomes active when you turn 18. Citizenship is required.

name: Project Pull
org: SF Public Utilities Commission and partner City departments
what_you_do: Paid summer internships in City departments for high school students, with a focus on STEAM careers and public service, such as architecture, business, engineering and science.
who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students (there are separate college tracks). The application page says details are coming soon.
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted on the page read)
deadline_text: The 2027 timeline on the application page says 'details coming soon'. Dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Use the High School Internship application page. Questions: sfprojectpull1996@gmail.com.
notes: The pages do not list age, pay or a deadline yet. Check the application page in early 2027.

name: YEP! Youth Employment Program
org: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department
what_you_do: First-job experience at rec centers and parks: arts, sports, aquatics, gardening, cooking and facility operations.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 in San Francisco.
pay_detail: Pay not posted on the page read
duration: Up to 25 hours per week in summer; 10 hours per week in the school year
deadline_text: No dates posted. Email the program to ask when the next round opens.
how_to_apply: Email yep@sfgov.org or call Yuri Ugarte at 415-452-3863.
notes: This page replaced the older Workreation name on the department site. An older listing says applicants need work-permit papers and no citizenship is required.

name: SFPL School-Year Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Help with children's and family programs at branch libraries. Openings listed include Ingleside, Noe Valley and North Beach (Cantonese or Mandarin speakers).
who_can_apply: No minimum age is listed for youth volunteers; if a branch is not on the application form it cannot take volunteers right now.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Ongoing; some roles start late October or early November
deadline_text: Rolling. Some positions start late October or early November 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form at https://on.sfpl.org/yva
notes: FOG Readers tutoring takes select volunteers age 15 and up (6 month commitment, needs fingerprinting). The same page lists paid teen jobs: YELL (summer, applications open each March) and the Youth Advisory Board (applications for this year closed Sept 14).

name: SSIP CityWorks (Sewer System Internship Program)
what_you_do: Paid summer internship at the SFPUC or a private engineering firm working on the sewer system, for students from southeast San Francisco neighborhoods.
who_can_apply: High school students from San Francisco's southeast neighborhoods; internships start after junior year.
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: No dates posted on the SFPUC page.
how_to_apply: The SFPUC page does not list an application. It says SFUSD students are referred through SFUSD's Career and Technical Education office, so ask them or the SFPUC workforce team.
notes: Narrow neighborhood focus (southeast San Francisco). The same SFPUC page also lists YouthWorks and Project Pull.

name: Teen Volunteer Programs (Nature Trail, Junior Zoologists, Leadership Fellows)
org: San Francisco Zoo and Gardens, Koret Animal Rescue and Conservation Center
what_you_do: Teen volunteering at the SF Zoo: Nature Trail (ages 12 to 14) shows small animals to guests; Junior Zoologists (15 to 17) help with animal care; Leadership Fellows (grades 10 to 12) help run Zoo Camp.
who_can_apply: Nature Trail: ages 12 to 14. Junior Zoologists: ages 15 to 17. Leadership Fellows: entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2026 (ages 15 to 17 per the zoo's volunteer page).
pay_detail: Volunteer program; pay not stated. Nature Trail and Junior Zoologists require buying a $40 uniform.
duration: Nature Trail: Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day, at least 7 days a month. Junior Zoologists: 2 days a month for 6 months. Leadership Fellows: Mon to Fri, 8:15 am to 4 pm, mid June to early Aug (2026: June 15 to Aug 7).
deadline_text: Nature Trail applications open each March (the page says 2027 applications open in March). Junior Zoologists and Leadership Fellows were closed on the pages read; 2026 Leadership Fellows group interviews were Apr 25, 2026. No 2027 closing dates posted.
how_to_apply: Each track has its own page. Nature Trail and Junior Zoologists include an online interview. Questions: naturetrail@sfzoo.org (Nature Trail), izvolunteer@sfzoo.org (Junior Zoologists), luked@sfzoo.org (Leadership Fellows), or (415) 753-7080.
notes: Located in San Francisco (a long trip from Sacramento). Applications were closed when checked. The Leadership Fellows page gave 2026 dates, so check for 2027 dates.

name: UCSF ImmunoExplore Summer Camp
what_you_do: Free summer camp at UCSF's Parnassus campus with lectures, games, Q&A sessions, patient panels and live anatomy dissections, mentored by UCSF students and faculty.
who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students who may have limited opportunities to engage with biomedical research, per the page. Grade range and other rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Not stated (summer camp; dates not posted)
deadline_text: The page says 2026 camper applications are open, but its title still reads Summer Camp 2025 and the summer 2026 camp has already passed. No 2027 dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Google Form linked from the ImmunoExplore page.
notes: Re-read the ImmunoX page on 2026-10-07. It is titled Summer Camp 2025 but mentions 2026 applications, so it may be out of date. Grades, camp dates and deadlines are not posted. The apply link is the Google Form linked on the page. Confirm dates and grade range with ImmunoX before applying.

name: UCSF SEP High School Intern Program
org: UCSF Science and Health Education Partnership
what_you_do: Eight week paid summer research internship at UCSF with a scientist mentor, plus college counseling and a trip to a college campus.
who_can_apply: Current juniors at an SFUSD high school or an SF public charter school, no exceptions. Grades and science background are not used to pick students; low-income and first-generation college students are encouraged.
pay_detail: $4,500 paid after completing the program (35 hours a week for 8 weeks)
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. Last cycle's deadline was Sunday, Feb 8 (the 2026 application). 2027 dates are not posted; fill in the page's interest form to be notified.
how_to_apply: Fill in the interest form to hear when the application opens, then submit the online application. About 50 students are interviewed for 25 spots; results come by email in April.
notes: The SEP high school programs page says 2025-26 is the final year of a program and that there will be no summer internship for 2026; it is not clear which program that means, while the intern page invites 2027 interest. Confirm with SEP at 415-364-8077.

name: Youth Art Exchange After-School Programs
what_you_do: Free after-school art programs led by professional artists for public high school students, building creative, technical and leadership skills.
who_can_apply: Mainly public high school students in San Francisco. Programs are free.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Contact YAX for current sessions.
how_to_apply: Call (415) 574-8137 or email info@youthartexchange.org.
notes: Also runs summer camps for grades 3 to 5 and classes for adults. The page does not mention paid internships or exact ages.

name: SF YouthWorks
org: City and County of San Francisco, run with JCYC and DCYF
what_you_do: Paid job readiness workshops and internships in City departments such as the SFPUC, the Public Library and SFO Airport, with mentoring and college tours.
who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders (rising juniors, rising seniors and graduating seniors) who live in or go to school in San Francisco and can get a work permit. Youth Leadership Team members must have finished a full YouthWorks session.
pay_detail: $19.61 per hour for school-year interns; $20.36 per hour for Youth Leadership Team members
deadline_text: The 2026-27 school-year application is closed (the DCYF newsletter listed Sept 14, 2026). The Youth Leadership Team application is marked coming soon. Summer dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the JCYC Workhub portal. Expect a short application and an interview step.
notes: Interns work in City departments such as the SFPUC, the Library and SFO. Former interns can return as paid Youth Leadership Team members. Ask JCYC about work permit help.

name: Teens Reach (San Jose Public Library teen council)
what_you_do: Teens ages 13 to 18 help with library programs (like kids crafts), sign up kids for Summer Learning and speak up as library advisors. Earn community service hours.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. You need a strong interest in the library, and you must go to meetings and join in activities.
deadline_text: Each branch has its own sign-up. No single deadline.
how_to_apply: Find your branch's Teens Reach sign-up on BetterImpact or ask the branch. Volunteer Services: 408-808-2181, volunteer.sjpl@sjlibrary.org.
notes: Meeting times differ by branch (for example Rose Garden Thursdays 4 p.m., Almaden Tuesdays 4:30 p.m.). Other SJPL teen roles include Teen Book Reviewer. TeenHQ is at the King Library, 150 E San Fernando.

name: SJSU Summer Session (Open University) for High School Students
city: San Jose, CA (online, hybrid and in person)
what_you_do: High school students can take SJSU summer college courses for credit through Open University without being admitted. More than 500 courses.
who_can_apply: High school students can register for summer classes through Open University without being admitted to SJSU.
pay_detail: Price not on the page; ask Summer Session (see SJSU Fees, Payment and Refund)
duration: 5 or 10 week sessions (2026: June 1 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: Summer 2026: Open University registration began April 15 and closed July 13. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Register as an Open University student using the first-time or returning student steps on the SJSU Summer registration page. Questions: professionaled@sjsu.edu or 408-924-2670.
notes: You pay college tuition. The page does not state age, grade or approval rules for high schoolers or the cost, so ask Summer Session. For fall and spring the page points to the Dual Enrollment Program (dualenrollment@sjsu.edu).

name: SkillsUSA
what_you_do: Career and technical education club with skills contests, leadership training and employer connections.
who_can_apply: Middle school, high school and college CTE students in a school chapter. Virtual chapters exist for students without a classroom chapter.
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the pages read; ask your CTE teacher.
deadline_text: Join through your CTE teacher. No cycle stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your CTE teacher, or use the 12 Steps to Start a Chapter or Virtual Chapter on skillsusa.org. Phone 844-875-4557, email customercare@skillsusa.org.
notes: Most useful if your school has a trades or tech CTE pathway.

name: SLAC Regional High School Science Bowl
org: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy National Science Bowl)
what_you_do: A team quiz competition on science and math at SLAC. Winning teams can move on to the national event. Volunteers are also needed.
who_can_apply: High school student teams registered by a coach or teacher. Team size and cost are not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Registration opened Oct 5, 2026. High school event is Feb 27, 2027 (middle school is Feb 6, 2027). Registration deadline not posted.
how_to_apply: A teacher or coach pre-registers the team on the National Science Bowl coach site (apps.orau.gov/nsb-coach). You do not need all team details for step one.
notes: Needs a school team and coach. Volunteer sign-up info is due to be shared by December 2026 (no experience needed). Event is at SLAC, 2575 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park.

name: SAGE Camp at SLAC
city: Menlo Park and Palo Alto, CA
what_you_do: Free one-week science camp for high schoolers from all backgrounds, held on the SLAC and Stanford campuses, with hands-on science.
who_can_apply: High school students from all backgrounds. The page lists no age, grade or residency limits. Apply on the Kaleidoscope platform.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 24 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Kaleidoscope platform linked from the SAGE site when the next cycle opens.
notes: The page says the camp is free. Whether it is overnight, and the 2027 dates, were not on the page I read. Check the SAGE site in February.

name: SMASH Residential (UC Berkeley site)
what_you_do: A free STEM program with a summer living at a university partner (UC Berkeley for the Bay Area), with computer science, college success and elective classes and mentors from STEM careers.
who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 with a 3.0 GPA, strong math scores, at a public or scholarship-funded private high school, with strong interest in computer science. Bay Area schools within the radius are preferred.
pay_detail: Free; tuition-free
duration: One year with a residential summer
deadline_text: Application dates for 2026 to 27 are not posted. Join the interest list for updates.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on smash.org/programs and watch for the application. Contact devo@smash.org.
notes: Based in Oakland (2148 Broadway). SMASH Virtual is a separate online option for a national audience; its cost is not stated. SMASH Morehouse is for males and SMASH Spelman for females.

name: Skyline College Dual Enrollment (San Mateo County CCD)
org: Skyline College, San Mateo County Community College District
what_you_do: Tuition-free college classes taken through your high school, so you earn high school and college credit at the same time.
who_can_apply: Students at partner high schools: Jefferson Union HSD, San Mateo Union HSD, South San Francisco USD, Sequoia Union HSD and Gateway charter school. Need a C or better to get college credit.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask your counselor about each term.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school (talk to your counselor), submit the Skyline application on CCCApply, then attend an enrollment workshop to register and get parent approval.
notes: Grades become part of a permanent college record and can affect financial aid and college admission. Contacts on the page: hendrieg@smccd.edu or fuentesa@smccd.edu. Canada College and College of San Mateo run their own dual enrollment pages, not checked here.

name: SMUD High School Internship Program
org: SMUD with Sacramento Employment and Training Agency (Sacramento Works)
what_you_do: Six-week paid summer internship at SMUD in areas such as IT, engineering, customer service, vehicle mechanics, accounting, HR and marketing.
who_can_apply: 16 or older (by June 2 in the 2026 cycle), current junior or senior, 2.5 GPA or higher, attends an eligible school in the SMUD service area, no relatives at SMUD, own transportation.
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour (2026), about 36 hours per week.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Mar 23, 2026 and closed May 1, 2026 (5 pm). 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Sacramento Works site before the deadline. Steps: application review, document check, computer random drawing (55 candidates), work readiness workshops and video interview, manager review, in-person interview. Up to 25 interns are chosen.
notes: Questions: SacramentoWorksFor.Youth@seta.net. Random drawing means even qualified students may not be picked. Check the school list on the Sacramento Works SMUD page. Age rule and school-area details come from the 2026 posting; confirm for 2027.

name: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
org: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI)
what_you_do: Mentored, hands-on summer research in health AI, working with real-world health data on problems at the intersection of AI and medicine.
who_can_apply: High school students, per the page. The page does not state age, grade range, residency or citizenship rules.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: Summer 2027 program. Application opens Nov 10, 2026 and closes Feb 1, 2027. Free online info session Tue Nov 10, 2026, 5 to 6 pm Pacific, open to students and parents.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application opens on Nov 10, 2026 (the page does not describe the form). Attend the free info session on Nov 10, 2026, or RSVP through the page. Questions: aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu.
notes: Re-read the AIMI page on 2026-10-07. The dates are for the Summer 2027 program. The page does not state pay or cost, length, detailed eligibility or whether the program is in person, so paid_type and needs_work_permit are placeholders until confirmed. Confirm those with aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu before applying. The Summer Health AI Bootcamp is a separate program on the same site and is not covered here.

name: Stanford CARE Explorers: AI x Precision Health
org: Stanford Center for Asian Health Research and Education
what_you_do: Two-week in-person summer program on health topics that affect Asian communities, AI basics and precision health data, with leadership skills.
who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors who are at least 14 and can commute daily to the Palo Alto campus. You need a laptop.
pay_detail: 2026 fee was $5,500; 2027 fee not announced. Limited need-based aid in 2026.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 sessions: June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17)
deadline_text: 2027 dates will be announced in fall 2026. Sign up for announcements.
how_to_apply: Sign up for application announcements on the CARE page; email carehighschoolprogram@stanford.edu.
notes: Pay-to-play. Day program, about 9am to 3pm on weekdays. No housing or transportation provided; lunch and snacks included. No application fee waivers in 2026.

name: Stanford Medicine Children's Health Teen Volunteer Program
org: Stanford Medicine Children's Health (Lucile Packard Children's Hospital)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers in five areas: mother and baby care, play and recreation, support services, education, and community-based activities.
who_can_apply: Teens. Start with an online orientation, then a scheduled interview; eligible teens get the application link after the interview. Age and schedule rules are given in the orientation.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
deadline_text: Openings and requirements are shown during the online orientation. No dates on the page.
how_to_apply: Start with the online orientation on volunteer.stanfordchildrens.org, then interview. Questions: volunteerservices@stanfordchildrens.org.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the page. Ask the volunteer office.

name: Genomics Research Internship Program at Stanford (GRIPS)
what_you_do: Eight-week summer genetics and genomics research in a Stanford lab, 4 hours a day, 5 days a week (about 20 hours a week).
who_can_apply: Live in Alameda, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara or Santa Cruz County; 16 or older by the start date; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; some biology, chemistry or programming background.
pay_detail: Application fee (amount not stated; waived for financial need). Stipend not stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, 5 days a week (2026: June 15 to Aug 6)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: opened Dec 2025, due Feb 28, 2026 at 11:59pm (fee waiver request due Feb 15). 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: 2026 process: email essays, transcripts, resume, science course list and one recommendation letter to grips-program@stanford.edu by the deadline.
notes: Decisions in 2026 came mid-March to mid-April. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year; check the page in December.

name: Stanford Health Care High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Non-clinical volunteer roles in the hospital, one shift a week for at least six months. It is not shadowing and does not count as clinical hours.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Inpatient unit roles need 18. Needs 6 to 8 hours of online training, a background check, a health screening (including a TB test), and orientation within 30 days of selection.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: At least 1 shift per week for 6 months (inpatient roles: 1 year)
deadline_text: The page says to use the portal to see the next application dates. Dates not shown on the page I read.
how_to_apply: Apply on volunteer.stanfordhealthcare.org. Questions: VolunteerResources@stanfordhealthcare.org or 650-723-7424.
notes: Stanford says this does not count for school clinical-hour needs and has no shadowing.

name: Stanford Clinical Summer Internship (MEDCSI)
what_you_do: Two-week hands-on medicine course with skills like ultrasound, dissection and suturing. This is a paid program for students, not a job.
who_can_apply: 16 by start; strongly suggested to have taken high school biology. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores, essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $6,580 on campus, $4,580 virtual, $2,480 for the 10-week fall virtual option. Application fee $95 for summer ($75 fall). Fee waivers for U.S. citizens or green card holders under $80,000 household income or in low-income support programs, limited and first come first served.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 13 to 24 on campus; July 27 to Aug 7 virtual)
deadline_text: All 2026 programs closed. The page says the next cycle opens Jan 1, 2027; no 2027 deadline posted. Last cycle: Nov 1, 2025 to Feb 9, 2026.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the MEDCSI SlideRoom portal when the new cycle opens. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores (if available), essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
notes: Pay-to-play and expensive. Fees shown are 2026 prices. No stipend or work experience. The program also admits undergraduate pre-med students.

name: Pediatrics Internship Program at Stanford (PIPS)
what_you_do: Seven-week summer internship in pediatrics at Stanford, about 30 hours a week, for students from nearby counties.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors, 16 or older, unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher, living in and attending high school in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Alameda, Contra Costa or Santa Cruz County. You must live with a family member or legal guardian; housing and transportation are not provided.
pay_detail: No fee. $3,000 stipend for students who show financial need.
duration: 7 weeks, 30 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Feb 23, 2026 (decisions Apr 1, 2026). 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the PIPS portal when the next cycle opens. Check the PIPS page for the next cycle.
notes: About 35 to 40 students are admitted. The page says in person, with some remote work possible. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
what_you_do: One live online college-style course, Monday to Friday for two weeks, for middle and high school students. You may take only one course per summer.
who_can_apply: Currently in grades 8 to 11 and between 13 and 19 years old during the program dates. Domestic and international students may apply.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.
duration: Two weeks, live online (2026: June 15 to 26 or July 6 to 17)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Mar 13, 2026 (decisions mid-May 2026). 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts and the application fee; rank up to three courses. Financial aid is a separate form due about a week after the deadline.
notes: Pay-to-play. Prices and dates are from 2026. The page says to join the mailing list for future dates. Age wording on the admissions page is 'between 13 and 19'.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
what_you_do: Eight weeks of full-time biomedical lab research with Stanford faculty and graduate student mentors, plus morning lectures at the start.
grades: Juniors and seniors (classes of 2027 and 2028 for the 2027 program)
who_can_apply: Juniors or seniors now (classes of 2027 and 2028), 16 or older by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the U.S., and a U.S. citizen or green card holder. Local Bay Area students are strongly favored. You must live with a family member or guardian.
pay_detail: No program cost. Most students get no stipend; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist. 2026 application fee was $50, waivable for family income under $80,000.
duration: 8 weeks, about 40 hours a week, tentatively June 7 to July 29, 2027
deadline_text: Application opens Dec 18, 2026 at 5pm Pacific; due late February 2027 (exact date not posted). 2026 deadline was Feb 21, 2026.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts and recommendations. In 2026 the decision date was Apr 10.
notes: Very competitive. Housing and transportation not provided. Fee and decision date shown are from the 2026 cycle.

name: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
what_you_do: Five-week, tuition-free summer program on Stanford's campus for juniors from low-income and first-generation backgrounds who want to explore medicine.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who are low-income and first-generation college students living in Northern California. About 24 students are admitted.
pay_detail: Tuition free. Housing and stipend not stated.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the SlideRoom link on the SMYSP page when it opens. Contact: smysp-team@stanford.edu.
notes: The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

name: City of Sunnyvale Youth Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Youth 13 and older can volunteer at special events, with office tasks, or with young people or seniors, including library roles.
who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. Most roles require volunteers 18 and older to be fingerprinted and cleared first, so ask which roles take teens.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Roles are posted as needed.
how_to_apply: Fill one application: general, library, or recreation and senior center. Volunteer Resources: 408-730-7533.
notes: Official page read directly. Fill out only one application.

name: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (SVCTE)
org: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (Metropolitan Education District)
what_you_do: Career technical classes for high school students in 22 pathways, including AI engineering, auto repair, culinary arts, nursing careers, HVAC, animation and fire science. Some give college credit or pre-apprenticeship.
who_can_apply: The pages read do not list eligibility rules. Shadow Days require your home school counselor's approval. Ask your counselor or call SVCTE about enrollment.
pay_detail: Not stated. Dual enrollment courses earn college credit. The site links a Schedule of Fees page that was not read, so ask about costs.
deadline_text: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your counselor for enrollment dates.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor about enrolling in SVCTE courses. To visit, apply for a Shadow Day through the SVCTE site (your counselor must approve it). Phone (408) 723-6403, Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. The site lists Milthon Marquez as Post-Secondary Planning Coach.
notes: Re-read the SVCTE home page and the Shadow Days, Dual Enrollment, Internships and Post-Secondary Options pages on 2026-10-07. The homepage lists 22 career technical courses (the old file said more than 24 pathways). Dual enrollment courses are taught by college professors at the high school campus. Shadow Days: after talking to your home school counselor, submit interest on the site; the counselor must approve it, and you get a confirmation 7 days before the visit. Eligibility, costs, deadlines and enrollment dates are not stated on the pages read.

name: The Tech Interactive Teen Volunteer Program (Holiday Helper)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers in the museum's Holiday Helper program, Nov 23, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027. The page does not describe the duties.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page states no minimum age or other rules.
deadline_text: Applications open Oct 9 to Oct 23, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer hub during the window. Questions: volunteer@thetech.org or 408-294-8324.
notes: Very time-sensitive: the window is two weeks. Check with the museum about age rules before applying.

name: Tri-Valley ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
what_you_do: Free career classes (30+ courses in about 10 career areas such as building trades, health science, IT and public services) for students in Dublin, Livermore and Pleasanton high schools.
who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is closed. Talk to your school's College and Career Specialist or counselor.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.

name: Trybe Summer Jobs and Paid Internships (East Oakland)
what_you_do: Skills building, leadership training and paid internships for East Bay youth. In the City's summer jobs list, Trybe offers a 100 hour summer job for East Oakland youth.
who_can_apply: East Bay youth. Trybe's old 2022 posting asked for age 16 or older with photo ID and SSN or ITIN, and offered a stipend option for under 16. Current rules are not posted.
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).
deadline_text: No current dates posted. The old 2022 posting took applications until May 31.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program
what_you_do: Volunteer in hospital and clinic areas such as patient transport, radiology and discharge for 1 to 2 four-hour shifts per week.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (at least one from a school mentor), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application completion deadline May 4, 2026 (first come, first served). 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.

name: UC Davis Medical Microbiology and Immunology high school research internship
org: UC Davis School of Medicine with DJUSD and Esparto CTE
what_you_do: A 10-week spring program on Tuesday afternoons: lab safety, pipetting, lab demos, 3D printing, and a visit to the Center for Valley Fever.
who_can_apply: Students in CTE programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
pay_detail: The DJUSD CTE page says its internships are unpaid. The UC Davis article does not mention pay.
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort not confirmed. Last known cohort ran Mar 18 to May 22, 2025.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows a UC Davis Center for Valley Fever internship in spring.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.

name: Summer at UC Davis Pre-College Program
org: UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education
what_you_do: Two-week on-campus summer program where you pick a subject (for example pre-med, forensics, equine science, startup entrepreneurship) and live in a UC Davis dorm.
grades: rising 9 to 12 (apply page); other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18
who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
pay_detail: 2025 tuition was $6,985 plus a $100 application fee (includes dorm and meals). 2027 price not posted yet.
duration: about 2 weeks per session (2025: July 7 to 18 and July 21 to Aug 1)
deadline_text: 2025 cycle deadline was May 16, 2025 (the fee page still shows 2025). 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.

name: UC Davis Upward Bound
what_you_do: Free college-prep help during the school year plus a summer program on the UC Davis campus.
who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
pay_detail: No fee listed on the page. Confirm with the program.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Check with an Upward Bound advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages read, so ask.

name: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
what_you_do: Six-week summer residential program. You work in a UC Davis lab with a faculty mentor on a real project and write a research paper.
who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $7,750 (housing, meals and 5 units of credit included). Application fee $45 in 2026. Fee reduction and application fee waiver available.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2026, teacher references by Mar 3. 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for fee reduction by the deadline if you need it.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.

name: UC Scout Online High School Courses
what_you_do: UC-approved online high school and AP courses that meet A-G requirements, self-paced.
who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
pay_detail: Fees vary by course; the site mentions free options for CA public schools and scholarships (prices not on the home page)
deadline_text: Fall 2026 enrollment is open (as of Oct 7, 2026).
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.

name: UCSF Health Volunteer Program (includes BCH Oakland campus)
org: UCSF Health / UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals
city: Oakland, CA (BCH Oakland) and San Francisco
what_you_do: Non-clinical hospital volunteering: visit and talk with patients, light clerical work, and help patients and visitors find their way. No shadowing, research or internships.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months
deadline_text: Page update dated Sept 22 (year not stated): registration opens Tuesday Oct 13 at 9:30am only for two high-need SF programs. Other opportunities, including others at BCH Oakland, are listed as full.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.

name: U.S. Senate Page Program
what_you_do: Paid job on the Senate floor and in offices while attending the Senate Page School, for one semester or the summer.
who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or rising junior or senior (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
deadline_text: Padilla's office: opens Oct 13, 2026, closes Oct 26, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office at Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Only about 30 positions in the whole Senate. Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.

name: United States Senate Youth Program
org: Hearst Foundations, with the California Department of Education
what_you_do: One week in Washington, DC meeting Senators and officials, with a $12,500 college scholarship. Two students are chosen per state, and all trip costs are paid.
grades: Juniors and seniors (rising juniors and seniors may apply)
who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations
deadline_text: California's deadline for the 2027 program is October 7, 2026 (today, as of this check). If you miss it, the next cycle is expected in fall 2027. States must report delegates by Dec 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.

name: USS Hornet Museum Volunteer (ages 16 and up)
org: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
what_you_do: Restore aircraft or the ship, work in the radio room, do outreach, or help visitors. Teens 16 and 17 work with an adult.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)
deadline_text: Rolling
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.

name: Valley Water Youth Commission
org: Valley Water (Santa Clara Valley Water District)
city: San Jose, CA (serves all Santa Clara County)
what_you_do: High school students from across Santa Clara County serve two-year terms on a youth commission for Valley Water. There are 21 seats, each appointed by one of the seven board members.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month
deadline_text: The application is closed and will open again in Spring 2027. Fill out the interest form to be told.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.

name: Virtual Enterprises International
what_you_do: A class where students run a simulated business, with trade shows, competitions and a Youth Business Summit.
who_can_apply: Students at partner schools. Schools join by filling out an interest form and talking with a VEI Regional Director.
pay_detail: School/district pays (cost not public)
deadline_text: Depends on your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school or counselor about the program. Contact info@veinternational.org or 855-740-6555.
notes: Not an individual sign-up; your school must be a partner. Cost to schools is not posted.

name: Washington Health (Fremont) High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Hospital volunteer roles for high school students at Washington Hospital in Fremont. Openings depend on what the hospital needs.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
deadline_text: Next high school round is Fall 2026. The waiting list closed May 22, 2026, but new students can still join and are contacted only when an info session is scheduled.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont.

name: Teen Heroes
org: City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: Summer mentoring and volunteer program. You help staff at city summer camps with set up, clean up, crafts, activities and special events.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 16, eligible West Sacramento residents. Needs proof of the hepatitis B vaccine series, fingerprinting and a background check.
pay_detail: Free to join, unpaid. The page does not list a stipend.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Dates for the next summer are not posted.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.

name: West Valley College Concurrent Enrollment
what_you_do: Students in grades 9 to 12 take West Valley College classes for free. Middle College and on-campus dual enrollment exist for some districts.
who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: grades 9 to 12. Middle College: juniors and seniors from LGSUHSD and CUHSD. Dual enrollment on high school campuses: CUHSD (Campbell Union High School District) students only.
pay_detail: Free (per the college page)
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Follow the college's term dates.
how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.

name: Wikipedia Editing
what_you_do: Anyone can edit Wikipedia, even without an account. Start with small fixes and use the tutorials.
who_can_apply: Open to almost anyone, even without logging in. The page links to guidance for younger editors but states no minimum age.
pay_detail: Free
deadline_text: Always open.
how_to_apply: Start editing, or make a free account (not required). Try The Wikipedia Adventure tutorial.
notes: Protect your personal info; do not share your school or address.

name: Woodland Community College Dual Enrollment (Yolo Community College District)
what_you_do: Free college classes for high school students: CCAP classes at partner high schools (eleven offer them, including Woodland, Pioneer, Winters) or classes online or on campus.
who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 8th grade (non-CCAP route). CCAP classes are offered at partner high schools; ask your counselor. Tuition is free for 11 units or fewer.
pay_detail: Free up to 11 units ($46 per unit fee waived); books may cost
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.

name: Teens Helping Seniors
what_you_do: Teens earn school community service credit by serving seniors in Woodland.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
deadline_text: No dates on the Teen Programs page.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Woodland Community Services registration portal (linked from the Teen Programs page) or call (530) 661-2000. Email: WoodlandCSD@cityofwoodland.gov.
notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

name: work2future Young Adult Program
what_you_do: Career advising, job readiness workshops, paid work experience and connections to employers for young people in Santa Clara County.
who_can_apply: Santa Clara County residents ages 16 to 24 who are low-income and have at least one barrier to employment or education.
pay_detail: Paid work experience; the page says earn up to $25 an hour. Other services are free.
deadline_text: Enrollment is open year-round.
how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program for ages 14 to 29, is also listed on the page. Income and barrier rules apply. Job centers may be open by appointment only.

name: West Sacramento Home Run Paid Summer Internships
org: West Sacramento Home Run and City of West Sacramento
what_you_do: Apply and interview for a paid summer internship with a local employer. The Home Run team gives work readiness training and the city pays you.
who_can_apply: Washington Unified School District high school students who are 16 by the first day. River City HS students need a Career Technical Education course; Yolo HS and Washington Middle College students need a teacher or counselor recommendation. Everyone attends one online info session.
pay_detail: Paid by the City of West Sacramento, up to 40 hours per week. Hourly rate not posted on the page.
duration: summer, up to 40 hours per week
deadline_text: The 2026 Internship Calendar is an image on the page (not readable here). 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Go to the Internships page, attend the info session, send the recommendation form if needed, then apply and interview with employers.
notes: Employers have included Center for Land Based Learning, Elica Health Centers, City of West Sacramento and others. The 2026 calendar on the page is an image, so ask for 2027 dates: wshomerun@cityofwestsacramento.org or (916) 617-4500.

name: YCOE Work-Based Learning (B-Unbound)
what_you_do: Pick a career interest, get matched by YCOE staff with a vetted mentor at a business, agency or nonprofit, and complete about 60 hours of hands-on learning.
who_can_apply: Students in Yolo County. Start through your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org. Age or grade limits were not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Stipend up to $500 on successful completion
deadline_text: Rolling; no posted deadline.
how_to_apply: Tell your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org.
notes: B-Unbound is the online platform for finding opportunities (interviews, tours, job shadowing, projects, internships). Placement depends on available mentors, so ask early. The stipend is paid after you finish the requirements. Email: CCR@ycoe.org.

name: Youth Employment Partnership (YEP) summer and afterschool jobs
what_you_do: Paid job training and work placements for Oakland youth, including summer programs (Oakland Summer Rising, Team Oakland, Career Try-Out) and afterschool jobs.
who_can_apply: Oakland youth. YEP's job training serves ages 14 to 24. The City of Oakland's summer list shows YEP's summer program for ages 14 to 18.
pay_detail: Paid; about 100 hours of work in the City summer program (hourly rate not posted)
duration: Summer: about 100 hours, June 1 to Sept 30 (City list). Afterschool jobs during the school year.
deadline_text: No closing dates posted. YEP lists an Afterschool Job Application and a Young Adult Program Application 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on yep.org/how-you-join, or call 510-533-3447 or visit 2300 International Blvd, Oakland.
notes: The YEP page does not give pay rates. Age 14 to 18 for summer comes from the City of Oakland table; the 19 to 24 programs are for older youth.

name: YMCA of San Francisco Workforce Development (Teens)
what_you_do: Teens 14 and older build job skills, get job readiness training and certifications, and may get paid internships and job placements. What is offered varies by YMCA branch.
who_can_apply: The page lists the program for ages 14 to 24 and older. Grade level, residency and other rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Paid internships are mentioned at the Urban Services YMCA. Wage and hours are not stated. Other activities are not described as paid.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The page says to contact the Workforce Development team. Phone numbers listed: Urban Services YMCA (415) 561-0631; Bayview Hunters Point YMCA (415) 822-7728; Chinatown YMCA (415) 576-9622.
notes: This is an umbrella page for several branch programs. Season, wage, hours and deadlines are not stated, so call a branch before a teen applies. The ymcasf.org/teens page lists teens ages 13-18 across programs, but it gives no details for Workforce Development. Contact emails on the page are obfuscated and were not confirmed, so none are listed.

name: Outdoor Science School Cabin Leader (Camp Campbell)
what_you_do: Teens mentor students during five-day outdoor science school sessions in the redwoods, guiding activities and helping keep camp safe and fun. Leaders get a full day of training before students arrive.
who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years old, in 10th grade or higher, and in good academic standing. A High School Authorization Form must be signed by members of your school. No prior training is required, according to the FAQ.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. The page says this is a way to earn Service-Learning credit for graduation.
duration: Five days per session (typically Monday to Friday). Session dates are not stated.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 school year open in August and close in the middle of May. The exact closing date is not stated.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application through the Learn More and Sign Up link, get a High School Authorization Form signed by members of your school, and watch email for further instructions. The page recommends applying at least two weeks before your session dates.
notes: Camp Campbell is at 16275 Highway 9, Boulder Creek, CA 95006, per the cabin-leaders page. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is needed. The same YMCA's Youth and Government program is already in ymca-silicon-valley-youth-and-government.json. Leaders in Training is also listed on the leadership page, but its age and details are not stated, so it is not a card.

name: California YMCA Youth & Government
city: Statewide program (listed by YMCA of Silicon Valley)
what_you_do: High school students model the California legislature and courts, build public speaking, writing and research skills, and can earn community service hours. The program has run for over 75 years.
who_can_apply: High school youth from throughout California, per the page. No other rules are stated.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page. Ask the YMCA.
deadline_text: Dates, fees and deadlines are not on the page.
how_to_apply: Click 'Sign up for more information' on the YMCA Leadership Development page, which opens the YMCA sign-up form. The page does not describe the application steps.
notes: Re-read the YMCA Leadership Development page on 2026-10-07. The same page lists Friday Night Live and Youth Technology Incubator Leadership Councils (separate teen groups), college tours and other teen programs; they are not part of this entry. The Model UN item on the page is for middle school students. Season, dates, cost and deadlines are not on the page, so confirm them with the YMCA before applying.

name: YMCA Youth and Government (Model Legislature and Court)
what_you_do: Weekly local meetings, then in-person conferences in November and February where teens act as legislators, lawyers and judges.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Join a local delegation. Cost and sign-up steps are not posted on the page.
pay_detail: Fee not posted on the page I read; ask your local YMCA about cost and scholarships
duration: Weekly meetings plus conferences in November and February
deadline_text: Sign-up dates are not stated on the page. A conference is planned for November, so ask now.
how_to_apply: Contact the program director at (626) 604-4210 or use the inquiry form on the YMCA of Orange County site.
notes: Over 1,300 teens in more than 60 California delegations. This page is run by the YMCA of Orange County (Southern California) and lists no Northern California contact. Ask the director which delegation serves your area, and ask about cost and scholarships.

name: Yolo County 4-H Youth Development Program
org: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources, Yolo County 4-H
what_you_do: Join a community 4-H club to do hands-on projects (animals, agriculture, arts, science), events and leadership roles.
