who_can_apply: Youth in Yolo County. The page does not list ages. Fee waivers are available.
pay_detail: 2026-27 enrollment is $80 per youth (waiver or reduction available).
deadline_text: 2026-2027 enrollment fee posted ($80). No closing date stated; join through a local club.
how_to_apply: Find a community club, attend a meeting, complete online enrollment and pay the fee. Office: bbrinkhoushatch@ucanr.edu, 530-666-8703.
notes: Teens can take leader and ambassador roles. Fee is non-refundable; a fee waiver or reduction form is available. Returning members update their online enrollment and submit health forms to their club.

name: Youth Employment Services (WIOA paid work experience)
what_you_do: Paid, WIOA-funded work experience with a local employer, plus help with job searches, resumes, interviews, and school or training options.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24, living in Yolo County, and not in school right now, per the program page. The page names foster care, homelessness, disabilities, parenting, leaving high school, and justice involvement as challenges the program serves.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate and number of hours are not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page. Contact the Workforce Development Program Manager to check eligibility and enrollment.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Development Program Manager at the Administrative Offices, (530) 757-5558, or drop by free office hours on Wednesdays from 3 to 6 p.m. at 2455 West Capitol Ave, #118, West Sacramento, CA 95691.
notes: Only the 17-year-old end of this guide's 13 to 18 range is covered. The page does not say whether a California work permit is needed for participants under 18, so ask. Older YCCA posts mention up to 300 paid hours; that figure is not on the current page and is not used here. Narrower and competitive: it is aimed at young people facing barriers and out of school.

name: Youth volunteers at Yolo County Library branches
city: Yolo County, CA (West Sacramento, Winters, Esparto, Clarksburg, Yolo and others)
what_you_do: Help library staff at a branch. A separate Youth Volunteer Application is available.
who_can_apply: Opportunities are limited and differ by branch. The Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch is not accepting applications right now. The page does not list a minimum age.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are accepted at branches.
how_to_apply: Download the Youth Volunteer Application (PDF) from the volunteer page and email it or drop it off at the branch you want.
notes: Call the branch first (main number 530-666-8005). The page said the Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch was not accepting volunteer applications when checked.

name: Youth volunteering at Yolo Food Bank
what_you_do: Help the food bank pack food and work at distributions. Volunteers ages 12 to 17 sign a youth waiver with a parent signature.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group. Ages 16 to 17 can volunteer alone with parent permission (youth waiver).
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts any time.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Yolo Food Bank volunteer site (with the Youth Volunteer Waiver for ages 12 to 17), then sign up online for events. Email volunteer@yolofoodbank.org.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and gloves at events. You log your own hours in your volunteer account. Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group.

name: Youth Community Service (YCS)
city: Palo Alto, CA (serves Palo Alto, East Palo Alto and nearby)
what_you_do: Nonprofit that connects youth with service projects, a peer mental health leadership program, school programs and a service award.
grades: Service award is for grades K to 12; Summer of Service is for high school
who_can_apply: For the Service Award: students in grades K to 12 who live or go to school in Santa Clara or San Mateo County. High schoolers need 100 hours within 12 months. Other programs list no clear age rule.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Service Award cycles run in four windows; the current one is Fall 2026, Sep 1 to Nov 30, 2026.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Do Service platform at volunteer.youthcommunityservice.org. Phone 650-858-8019 or email ycs@youthcommunityservice.org.
notes: Also offers a scholarship and one-day service pop-ups. Based at 780 Arastradero Rd, Palo Alto.

name: Youth Radio
what_you_do: Youth media group: learn journalism, audio storytelling and digital content, with editors as mentors. Teens keep control of their own stories.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. No experience needed.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the site
deadline_text: No dates posted. Youth Radio paused in 2024 and says it is back in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on youthradio.org.
notes: The page describes training and mentoring, not a formal paid internship. Ask whether it is paid. It is not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.

name: Youth Spirit Artworks job training
what_you_do: Arts training and paid jobs for low-income and homeless youth.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 25, low-income or homeless youth (per the Berkeley Public Library jobs page).
deadline_text: Not posted
how_to_apply: Email jobtraining@youthspiritartworks.org or call 510-858-7229.
notes: Ages and contact come from the library page. The group's home page shows free arts workshops and drop-in events for ages 14 to 25 but no job training details, so ask about jobs. Not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.

name: Youth UpRising Summer Jobs and Job Readiness
what_you_do: Job readiness training and paid summer jobs or internships for East Oakland youth, plus career and education services all year.
who_can_apply: East Oakland youth. The City of Oakland list shows YU summer jobs for ages 14 to 21. YU serves ages 13 to 24 overall.
pay_detail: Paid (100 hours of fully paid work per the City list); rate not posted
duration: About 100 hours over 4 to 6 weeks (City list)
deadline_text: No dates posted on the site. Contact YU in spring for the next summer.
how_to_apply: Call 510-777-9909 or visit 8711 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The site gives no online form.
notes: YU's own site has no summer job details, so the ages and hours come from the City of Oakland's 2026 list. Also a referral partner for EBMUD's high school internship.

name: YouthBeat Media Careers and Pre-Apprentice Program
what_you_do: Free media training in classrooms and afterschool clubs. Advanced students can join a pre-apprentice program and paid fee-for-service projects at YouthBeat PRO.
who_can_apply: Oakland middle and high school students. The City summer jobs list shows Media Careers for ages 16 to 21 (June to September).
pay_detail: Training is free; apprentice and PRO work is paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Use the Apply link on the site.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page at youthbeat.org/apply, or call 510-922-0060 or email youthbeatmedia@gmail.com.
notes: YouthBeat's own page does not state exact ages; 16 to 21 comes from the City of Oakland's list. Address is a PO box in Oakland.

name: Zooniverse Citizen Science
what_you_do: Help real researchers by classifying images, audio and text for hundreds of online projects.
who_can_apply: Open to volunteers online. The pages read state no age rule; check the user agreement.
pay_detail: No cost stated on the pages read; it is a volunteer research site
deadline_text: Always open.
how_to_apply: Go to zooniverse.org, pick a project, and make an account if the project asks.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the home page or FAQ. Projects span arts, biology, climate, history, language, medicine, nature, physics, space and social science.
